SPECIFICATIONS

The rear seats have a backrest with a structure guaranteed to ensure maximum safety for the occupants through a metal partition designed to prevent any objects in the luggage compartment entering the passenger compartment in the case of an impact.

In order to increase the capacity of the luggage compartment, a split folding rear seat (40%/60%) is available on request.

The rear cushions have a pressed steel base with a structure that ensures an anti-submarining effect.

There are three height adjustable head restraints that are operated manually.

The head restraints can be placed in the lowest position through a single, electrically controlled action, increasing rear visibility.

There is an armrest, on the backrest, between the two side seats, that opens and can be folded back. There are buttons in the housing for operating the seat heating function, the sun blind and the sliding of the right front seat (where fitted). Access to the ski holder compartment is possible with the armrest lowered.

The outer sides of the backrest have two padded covers in keeping with the style of the backrest. They house the Side Bag modules which are designed to protect the chest of the occupants in the case of side impacts.

COMPOSITION

COMFORT SEATS

Adaptation and massage function

The adaptation and massage functions are produced using the same component. This component is a system comprising air bags, located between the cover and the upholstery.

The quantity of air contained inside the bags is managed by an electronic control unit in order to produce the optimum pressure distribution depending on the dimensions, weight and position of the occupant of the seat. The massage function is produced by partly inflating and deflating the bags according to a predefined cycle.

System features

The "Adaptation" and "Massage" function management system components are:

  • an electronic control unit comprising an electronic card and pneumatic vales which have the function of regulating the amount of air in the individual bags;
  • an air pump;
  • air bags located in the cushion in the front and side areas and in the backrest in the lumbar region;
  • the wiring, connecting the electronic control unit and the air pump, the supply leads and the control signal transmission cables;
  • the pneumatic connecting pipes between the electronic control unit valves and the air bags and between the electronic control unit and the air pump.

The adaptation function is activated when the occupant requests by pressing the function button for about two seconds.

This activation features:

  • an initial stage for completely inflating the bags;
  • a second deflation stage controlled according to the pressure exerted by the occupant until an optimum distribution situation is reached, lasting about 30 secs.

When the best configuration is produced, the pressure distribution is read/checked every four minutes with a new adjustment of the amount of air in the bags.

The massage is carried out when the occupant requests and lasts four minutes, after which the system carries out an adaptation stage and then a new massage cycle until the occupants switches the massage control off.

The system moves to the adaptation regime and the "adaptation off" control must be selected to switch it off permanently.

The lumbar support can be adjusted, to a certain extent, whilst the massage function is in progress.

The massage and adapation functions cannot be activated simultaneously the same as for the front seat. if the occupants have switched both functions on then the system will give priority to the massage function.

Any "adapation on" signal is ignored during this cycle.

When the ignition key is turned off, the system ends the massage and adaptation functions cycle.

When the vehicle is started up again, the "adaptation" or "massage" function has to be reselected whilst the lumbar support function setting is maintained.

The massage cycle sequence is as follows:

  • 1 left and right rear areas (simultaneously)
  • 2 lower lumbar support
  • 3 upper lumbar support
  • 4 lower lumbar support
  • 5 left and right rear areas (simultaneously)

The bags are activated alternately, i.e. the cycle goes in increasing order from point 1 to point 5 and then in decreasing order from point 5 to point 1.
